target.title: fix(channels): normalize phone identities with stray plus signs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where phone-based channel identities could normalize to invalid values when input contained doubled or embedded `+` characters. In WhatsApp self-chat, allowlist, and phone-derived routing flows, equivalent phone numbers could fail to match if an operator copied a number with an extra plus sign or pasted a phone-like value with punctuation in the wrong place.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared `normalizeE164` helper now strips provider prefixes, keeps digits only, returns `+<digits>` for phone-like input, and returns an empty string when no digits remain. This preserves the existing loose E.164 contract while avoiding invalid `+...+...` identities across WhatsApp, Signal, iMessage, and other SDK callers.

This intentionally changes the exported Plugin SDK behavior for invalid/noisy phone input. The old `+` and embedded-plus outputs were not usable sender identities, and callers that already treat an empty normalized value as invalid now fail closed instead of comparing against a truthy non-phone identity.

The WhatsApp setup test mock was updated to mirror the shared helper so setup tests no longer preserve the old normalization bug.

## User Impact

Users who configure phone-based allowlists or self-chat behavior get more reliable matching when phone numbers include common copy/paste noise. A malformed-but-recoverable value like `++1234567890` or `1+234+567` now resolves to the same canonical identity as the clean number, so the bot is less likely to silently ignore an authorized sender or miss self-chat mode.

Invalid phone text no longer becomes the truthy identity `+`, which avoids storing or comparing against a value that cannot represent a real sender.

## Evidence

- Real after-fix helper proof:

  ```shell
  $ node --import tsx -e 'const { normalizeE164 } = await import("./src/utils.ts"); for (const input of ["++1234567890", "1+234+567", "not a phone number"]) console.log(`${JSON.stringify(input)} -> ${JSON.stringify(normalizeE164(input))}`);'
  "++1234567890" -> "+1234567890"
  "1+234+567" -> "+1234567"
  "not a phone number" -> ""
  ```

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/utils.test.ts` passed: 23/23 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/channel.setup.test.ts` passed: 18/18 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Structured review found no actionable regressions.
- Installed Crabbox `0.36.0` and Blacksmith CLI `0.4.46`, but remote Testbox proof is blocked because this machine is not authenticated with Blacksmith. Direct AWS Crabbox is also blocked by missing broker/AWS auth.
- AI assistance: Codex was used to implement and review this change.
